title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: CHAPTER XXIII. JUST IN TIME

title: The Green Mummy
text: Of all the surprises in connection with the tragedy of the green

title: The Green Mummy
text: mummy, this was surely the greatest. Sidney Bolton had undoubtedly been

title: The Green Mummy
text: murdered for the sake of the emeralds, and the assassin had escaped

title: The Green Mummy
text: with the spoil, for which he had sold his soul. Yet here was one of the

title: The Green Mummy
text: jewels returned anonymously to Random, who could pass on the same to its

title: The Green Mummy
text: rightful owner. In the midst of his amazement Sir Frank could not help

title: The Green Mummy
text: chuckling when he thought how enraged Professor Braddock would be at Don

title: The Green Mummy
text: Pedro's good fortune. At the eleventh hour, as it were, the Peruvian had

title: The Green Mummy
text: got back his own, or at least a portion of his own.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Placing the emerald in his drawer, Random gave orders to his servant

title: The Green Mummy
text: that the sentry, when off duty, should be brought before him. Just as

title: The Green Mummy
text: Random finished dressing for mess--and he dressed very early, so as to

title: The Green Mummy
text: devote his entire attention to solving this new problem--the soldier who

title: The Green Mummy
text: had been on guard appeared. But he could tell nothing more than he had

title: The Green Mummy
text: already related. When doing sentry-go immediately outside the gate of

title: The Green Mummy
text: the Fort, the packet had been slipped into the box, while the man was at

title: The Green Mummy
text: the far end of his beat. It was quite dark when this was done, and the

title: The Green Mummy
text: soldier confessed that he had not heard a sound, much less had he seen

title: The Green Mummy
text: anyone. The person who had brought the glorious gem had watched his

title: The Green Mummy
text: opportunity, and, soft-footed as a cat, had stolen forward in the

title: The Green Mummy
text: darkness to drop the precious parcel on the floor of the sentry box.

title: The Green Mummy
text: There the man had found it by the feel of his feet, when he stepped in

title: The Green Mummy
text: some time later to escape a shower. But what time had elapsed from the

title: The Green Mummy
text: placing of the parcel to its discovery by the sentry it was impossible

title: The Green Mummy
text: to say. It must, however, as Random calculated, have been within the

title: The Green Mummy
text: hour, since, before then, it would not have been dark enough to hide

title: The Green Mummy
text: the approach of the person, whether male or female, who carried a king's

title: The Green Mummy
text: ransom in the brown paper parcel.

title: The Green Mummy
text: At first Random was inclined to place the sentry under arrest for having

title: The Green Mummy
text: failed so much in his duty as to allow anyone to approach so near the

title: The Green Mummy
text: Fort; but, as he had already reprimanded the man, and, moreover, wished

title: The Green Mummy
text: to keep the fact of the recovered jewel quiet, he simply dismissed him.

title: The Green Mummy
text: When alone, he sat down before the fire, wondering who could have dared

title: The Green Mummy
text: so very greatly, and for what reason the emerald had been handed to

title: The Green Mummy
text: him. If it had been sent to Don Pedro, or even to Professor Braddock, it

title: The Green Mummy
text: would have been much more reasonable.

title: The Green Mummy
text: It first occurred to him that Mrs. Jasher, out of gratitude for the way

title: The Green Mummy
text: in which he had treated her, had sent him the jewel. Remembering his

title: The Green Mummy
text: former experience, he smelt the parcel, but could detect no sign of the

title: The Green Mummy
text: famous Chinese scent which had proved a clue to the letter. Of course

title: The Green Mummy
text: the direction on the packet and the inscribed slip of paper were in

title: The Green Mummy
text: feigned handwriting, so he could gather nothing from that. Still, he

title: The Green Mummy
text: did not think that Mrs. Jasher had sent the emerald. She was desperately

title: The Green Mummy
text: hard up, and if she had become possessed of the gem by murder--presuming

title: The Green Mummy
text: her to have been the woman who talked to Bolton through the window--she

title: The Green Mummy
text: assuredly would have sold it to supply her own needs. Certainly, if

title: The Green Mummy
text: guilty, she would still possess the other emerald, of equal value; but

title: The Green Mummy
text: undoubtedly, had she risked her neck to gain a fortune, she would

title: The Green Mummy
text: have kept the entire plunder which was likely to cost her so dear. No;

title: The Green Mummy
text: whomsoever it was who had repented at the eleventh hour, Mrs. Jasher was

title: The Green Mummy
text: not the person.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Perhaps Widow Anne was the woman who had talked through the window, and

title: The Green Mummy
text: who had restored the emerald. But that was impossible, since Mrs. Bolton

title: The Green Mummy
text: habitually took more liquor than was good for her, and would not have

title: The Green Mummy
text: the nerve to deliver the jewel, much less commit the crime, the more

title: The Green Mummy
text: especially as the victim was her own son. Of course she might have

title: The Green Mummy
text: found out Sidney's scheme to run away with the jewels, and so would have

title: The Green Mummy
text: claimed her share. But if she had been in Pierside on that evening--and

title: The Green Mummy
text: her presence in Gartley had been sworn to by three or four cronies--she

title: The Green Mummy
text: would have guessed who had strangled her boy. If so, not all the jewels

title: The Green Mummy
text: in the world would have prevented her denouncing the criminal. With

title: The Green Mummy
text: all her faults--and they were many--Mrs. Bolton was a good mother, and

title: The Green Mummy
text: looked upon Sidney as the pride and joy of her somewhat dissipated life.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Mrs. Bolton was certainly as innocent as Mrs. Jasher.

title: The Green Mummy
text: There remained Hervey. Random laughed aloud when the name came into

title: The Green Mummy
text: his puzzled head. That buccaneer was the last person to surrender his

title: The Green Mummy
text: plunder or to feel compunction in committing a crime. Once the skipper

title: The Green Mummy
text: got his grip on two jewels, worth endless money, he would never let them

title: The Green Mummy
text: go--not even one of them. Arguing thus, it seemed that Hervey was out of

title: The Green Mummy
text: the running, and Random could think of no one else. In this dilemma he

title: The Green Mummy
text: remembered that two heads were better than one, and, before going into

title: The Green Mummy
text: dinner, he sent a note to Archie Hope, asking him to come to the Fort as

title: The Green Mummy
text: speedily as possible.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Sir Frank was somewhat dull at dinner on that evening, and scarcely

title: The Green Mummy
text: responded to the joking remarks of his brother officers. These jocularly

title: The Green Mummy
text: put his preoccupation down to love, for it was an open secret that the

title: The Green Mummy
text: baronet admired the fair Peruvian, although no one as yet knew that

title: The Green Mummy
text: Random was legally engaged with Don Pedro's consent. The young man

title: The Green Mummy
text: good-humoredly stood all the chaff hurled at him, but seized the

title: The Green Mummy
text: opportunity to slip away to his quarters as soon as coffee came on the

title: The Green Mummy
text: table and the smoking began. It was nine o'clock before he returned to

title: The Green Mummy
text: his room, and here he found Hope waiting for him impatiently.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I see you have been dining at the Pyramids,” said Random, seeing that

title: The Green Mummy
text: Hope was in evening dress.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Archie nodded.

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: the Professor asked me to dinner to talk over matters.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “What does he say?” asked Random, looking for the cigarette box.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Oh, he is very angry with Mrs. Jasher, and considers that she has

title: The Green Mummy
text: swindled him. He called to see her this afternoon, and--so he says--had

title: The Green Mummy
text: a stormy interview with her.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I don't wonder at that, if he speaks as he generally does,” said the

title: The Green Mummy
text: other grimly, and pushing along the cigarettes, “There you are! The

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: me what the Professor intends to do.”

text: “Well,” said Archie, turning half round from the side table where he

title: The Green Mummy
text: was pouring out the whisky, “he had already started action, by sending

title: The Green Mummy
text: Cockatoo to live at the Sailor's Rest and spy on Hervey.”

text: “What rubbish! Hervey is, going away to-morrow in The Firefly, bound for

title: The Green Mummy
text: Algiers. Nothing is to be learned from him.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “So I told the Professor,” said Hope, returning to the armchair near the

title: The Green Mummy
text: fire, “and I mentioned that Don Pedro had induced the skipper to write

title: The Green Mummy
text: out a full account of the theft of the mummy from Lima thirty years

title: The Green Mummy
text: ago. I also said that the signed paper would be handed in at the Gartley

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Humph! And what did Braddock say to that?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Nothing much. He merely stated that whatever Hervey said toward proving

title: The Green Mummy
text: the ownership of your future father-in-law, that he intended to stick

title: The Green Mummy
text: to the embalmed corpse of Inca Caxas, and also that he intended to claim

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: Random rose and went to the drawer of his desk.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I am afraid he has lost one emerald, at all events,” he said, unlocking

title: The Green Mummy
text: the drawer.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “What's that?” said Hope sharply. “Why did you--oh, gosh!” He jumped up

title: The Green Mummy
text: with an amazed look as Random held up the magnificent gem, from which

title: The Green Mummy
text: streamed vividly green flames in the mellow lamplight. “Oh, gosh!”

title: The Green Mummy
text: gasped the artist again. “Where the devil did you get that?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I sent for you to tell you,” said Sir Frank, giving the jewel into his

title: The Green Mummy
text: friend's hand and coming back to his seat. “It was found in the sentry

title: The Green Mummy
text: box.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: Hope stared at the great jewel and then at the soldier.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “What do you mean by that?” he demanded. “How the dickens could it be

title: The Green Mummy
text: found in a sentry box? You must be making a mistake.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Not a bit of it. It was found on the floor of the box by the sentry, as

title: The Green Mummy
text: I tell you, and I have sent to consult with you as to how the deuce it

title: The Green Mummy
text: got there.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Hervey,” muttered Archie, fascinated by the gem.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Random shrugged his square shoulders.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Catch that Yankee Shylock returning anything he got his grip on, even

title: The Green Mummy
text: as a wedding present.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “A wedding present,” said Hope, more at sea than ever. “If you don't

title: The Green Mummy
text: mind giving me details, old chap, my head would buzz less.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I rather think that it will buzz more,” said Random dryly, and,

title: The Green Mummy
text: producing the brown paper in which the gem had been wrapped, and the

title: The Green Mummy
text: inscribed paper found within, he related all that had happened.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Archie listened quietly and did not interrupt, but the puzzled look on

title: The Green Mummy
text: his face grew more pronounced.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Well,” ended Random, seeing that no remark was made when he had

title: The Green Mummy
text: finished, “what do you think?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Lord knows! I'll go out of my mind if these sort of things come along.

title: The Green Mummy
text: I am a simple sort of chap, and have no use for mysteries which beat all

title: The Green Mummy
text: the detective stories I have ever read. That sort of thing is all very

title: The Green Mummy
text: well in fiction, but in real life--humph! What are you going to do?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Give back the emerald to Don Pedro.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Of course, though, it is given to you for a wedding present. And then?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Then”--Random stared into the fire--“I don't know. I asked you in to

title: The Green Mummy
text: assist me.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Willingly; but how?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: Random pondered for a few moments.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Who sent that emerald to me, do you think?” he asked, looking squarely

title: The Green Mummy
text: at the artist.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Hope meditatively turned the jewel in his long fingers.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Why not ask Mrs. Jasher?” he suggested suddenly.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “No!” Sir Frank shook his head. “I fancied it might be her, but it

title: The Green Mummy
text: cannot be. If she is guilty--as she must be, should she have sent the

title: The Green Mummy
text: emerald--she would not part with her plunder when she is so hard up.

title: The Green Mummy
text: I am beginning to believe, Hope, that what she said was true about the

title: The Green Mummy
text: letter.”

text: “How do you mean exactly?”

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: with such a flimsy lock it was unsafe, but the baronet shook his head.

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: jewel of this description in my quarters. Well,” he came back to his

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: puzzles me.”

text: “Why not do as I suggest and go to Mrs. Jasher? In any case you are

title: The Green Mummy

text: “Yes. I want to decide what to do about the woman. I had intended to go

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I shall be delighted. What do you intend to do?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “She doesn't deserve it,” replied Hope, lighting a fresh cigarette.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Does anyone ever deserve anything?” asked Sir Frank cynically. “What

title: The Green Mummy
text: does Miss Kendal think of the business? I suppose Braddock told her. He

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “He told her at dinner, when I was present. Lucy is quite on your side.

title: The Green Mummy
text: She says that she had known Mrs. Jasher for months and that there is

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

text: “Why did you prevent her?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: Archie colored.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I daresay I am a trifle prudish,” he replied, “but after what has

title: The Green Mummy
text: happened I do not wish Lucy to associate with Mrs. Jasher. Do you blame

title: The Green Mummy

text: “No, I don't. All the same, I don't think that Mrs. Jasher is an immoral

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Perhaps not; but we needn't discuss her character, as we know precious

title: The Green Mummy
text: little of her past, and she no doubt told you the story that best suited

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: evening, and then send her away with a sum of money in her pocket to

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I shall help her certainly,” said Random, with his eyes on the fire,

title: The Green Mummy
text: “but can't say exactly how. It is my opinion that the poor wretch is

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “You are a soldier with a conscience, Random.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: The other laughed.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Why shouldn't a soldier have a conscience? Do you take your idea

title: The Green Mummy
text: of officers from the lady novelist, who makes us out to be all idle

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Of course. I'm with you right along, as Hervey would say. But first,

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Oh, yes, you would. The greater the sinner the more need she or he

title: The Green Mummy
text: has of help, you know, my dear fellow. But get your coat on, and let us

title: The Green Mummy

text: Sir Frank laughed, as, aided by the artist, he struggled into his

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy

text: “We would rather stay here in San Remo,” said Mrs. Hope, becoming

title: The Green Mummy
text: slightly pale. “Don't think me unkind, Inez, but I could not bear to

title: The Green Mummy
text: go to Peru. It is associated too much in my own mind with that terrible

title: The Green Mummy
text: green mummy.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Oh, Don Pedro has taken that back to the Andes,” explained Sir Frank,

title: The Green Mummy
text: “and it is now reposing in the sepulchre in which it was placed,

title: The Green Mummy
text: hundreds of years ago, by the Indians, faithful to Inca Caxas. Inez and

title: The Green Mummy
text: I are going up to a kind of forbidden city, where Don Pedro reigns as

title: The Green Mummy
text: Inca, and I expect we shall have a jolly time. I hear there is some big

title: The Green Mummy
text: game shooting there.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “What about your soldiering?” asked Hope, rather, surprised at this

title: The Green Mummy
text: extended tour being arranged.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Oh, my husband has left the army,” pouted Inez. “His duties kept him

title: The Green Mummy
text: away from me nearly all the day, and I grew weary of being left alone.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “So you see, Mrs. Hope,” laughed Random gayly, “that I have had to

title: The Green Mummy
text: succumb to my fireside tyrant. We shall go and see this fairy city and

title: The Green Mummy
text: then return to my home in Oxfordshire. There Inez will settle down as

title: The Green Mummy
text: a real English wife and I'll turn a country squire. So, after all our

title: The Green Mummy
text: troubles, peace will come.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “And as you will not come to my country,” said Lady Random to her

title: The Green Mummy
text: hostess, “you cannot refuse to visit Frank and myself at the Grange.

title: The Green Mummy
text: We have had so much trouble together that we cannot lose sight of each

title: The Green Mummy
text: other.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “No,” said Lucy, kissing her. “We will come to Oxfordshire.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: So it was arranged, and the next day Mr. and Mrs. Hope went over to

title: The Green Mummy
text: Monte Carlo to see the last of Sir Frank and his wife. They stood on

title: The Green Mummy
text: the heights watching the pretty little steamer making for South America.

title: The Green Mummy
text: Archie noticed that his wife's face was somewhat sad.

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Are you sorry we did not go, sweetheart?”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “No,” she replied, placing her arm within his own. “I only want to be

title: The Green Mummy
text: with you.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “That is all right.” He patted her hand. “Now that we have sold all the

title: The Green Mummy
text: furniture in the Pyramids, and have got rid of the lease, there will be

title: The Green Mummy
text: nothing to remind you of the green mummy.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “Yet I can't help thinking of my unfortunate step-father, and of poor

title: The Green Mummy
text: Mrs. Jasher, and of Sidney Bolton. Oh, Archie, little as we can afford

title: The Green Mummy
text: it, I am glad that we allow Mrs. Bolton a small sum a year. After all,

title: The Green Mummy
text: it was through my step-father that her son met with his death.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I don't quite agree with you, dear. Cockatoo's innate savagery was the

title: The Green Mummy
text: cause, as Professor Braddock did not intend or desire murder. But there,

title: The Green Mummy
text: dear, do not think any more about these dismal things. Dream of the time

title: The Green Mummy
text: when I shall be the president of the Royal Academy, and you my lady.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “I am your lady now. But,” added Lucy, perhaps from an association of

title: The Green Mummy
text: ideas of color and the Academy, “I shall hate green for the rest of my

title: The Green Mummy
text: life.”

title: The Green Mummy
text: “That's unlucky, considering it is Nature's color. My dear, in a year or

title: The Green Mummy
text: two this tragedy, or rather the three tragedies, will seem like a dream.

title: The Green Mummy
text: I won't listen to another word now. The green mummy has passed out of

title: The Green Mummy
text: our lives and has taken its bad luck with it.”

title: The Green Mummy

title: The Green Mummy
text: leaving all their sorrows behind them, while the smoke of the steamer

title: The Green Mummy
